Candidate 0 is the strongest default: visible arrival order, simple staffing, accessible place preservation and emergency-route protection. Cohorts could improve turnover but require safe clearing; registers, priority shares and draws add administrative or dispute burdens.

Candidates 6 and 7 repair existing mechanisms rather than create new ones. Candidate 8 adds voluntary departure prompting as its primary intervention. Candidate 5 is conditionally usable only with credible turnover information, as explicitly required; it must otherwise not be trialed. No candidate definitely violates a hard constraint.

pair.reason: B6 narrowly improves on A0 by specifying when joining stops, preventing untracked overflow, defining reopening and recording displaced demand. These make emergency-access protection and its fairness costs more inspectable without adding substantial staffing complexity.
